name: Typedream
tagline: Create a simple responsive landing site from text-first blocks and publish it

tiers.name: Free
tiers.limits: 1 published page, 1 seat, Typedream.app domain and badge; 5% transaction fee plus card or PayPal fees

tiers.name: Launch
tiers.limits: Unlimited pages, 1 CMS/blog collection, 1,000 form submissions, 1,000 email subscribers and 2 collaborators; 2% transaction fee
tiers.notes: Includes one free .xyz domain for the first year.

tiers.name: Grow
tiers.limits: Unlimited pages, CMS/blog collections and form submissions, 5,000 email subscribers, 5 collaborators and password protection; 2% transaction fee
tiers.notes: Includes one free .xyz domain for the first year.

pricing.freeTierCaps: 1 published page, 1 seat, Typedream.app subdomain and badge; selling incurs 5% plus payment-processing fees
pricing.billingTerms: monthly + annual; subscriptions auto-renew per site and annual prices are effective monthly rates
pricing.hiddenCosts: Typedream takes 5% of sales on Free and 2% on both paid plans in addition to card/PayPal processing; each site needs its own subscription, and the included .xyz domain is free only for year one.

verdictSummary: The core loop is small enough for a capable coding agent to produce a useful local version in one sitting. For Typedream, create a simple responsive landing site from text-first blocks and publish it. The hard boundary is hosted editing, forms, analytics, domains, and polished templates, plus editor polish, hosting, templates, and ecosystem.
coreLoopDIY: Assemble a simple responsive landing site from text-first blocks, edit copy and media, preview breakpoints, and publish a static site to a user-owned target.
whatYouLose: hosted editing, forms, analytics, domains, and polished templates
moatNotes: editor polish, hosting, templates, and ecosystem
ongoingBurden: responsive rendering, forms, domains, certificates, deploys, backups, template maintenance, and browser regressions
whyPeopleStillPay: People still pay for Typedream because the page renderer is reproducible, but customers pay to avoid becoming their own hosting and browser-compatibility team. The recurring cost buys responsive rendering, forms, domains, certificates, deploys, backups, template maintenance, and browser regressions, not just the visible interface.

priorArt.name: Webstudio
priorArt.desc: Open-source visual website builder designed around web standards.

alternatives.name: Mobirise AI
alternatives.desc: Prompt-assisted block sites, hosting and code export free for three projects a month.

facts.install: Browser signup; projects can be hosted by Mobirise or exported as HTML, CSS and JavaScript
facts.engines: Proprietary text-to-site, copy, image and video generation; the underlying model providers are not disclosed
facts.dataFormat: Projects are saved in the hosted builder; export downloads ordinary HTML, CSS, JavaScript and asset files
facts.gapVsPaid: Mobirise AI is prompt-and-block driven rather than a clean text-first editor, and free creation is capped at three new sites monthly.
facts.setupBlocker: The permanent free allowance is capped at three distinct generated/exported projects per month

alternatives.name: Plasmic
alternatives.desc: Hosted blocks, responsive design and custom domains free; dramatically more knobs than Typedream.

facts.install: Hosted signup; optional npm-installed Plasmic CLI for React code generation and deployment in your own repository
facts.engines: Plasmic AI (beta); the official site does not name its underlying model provider
facts.dataFormat: Hosted projects and CMS records in Plasmic Cloud; codegen writes React components plus plasmic.json and plasmic.lock into the user's repository
facts.gapVsPaid: Plasmic is dramatically more complex than Typedream's text-first editor, so a simple landing page takes more decisions.
facts.setupBlocker: Free hosted output keeps Plasmic branding; codegen/self-deployment requires a Node/React project and deployment workflow

alternatives.name: Publii
alternatives.desc: A desktop block editor that publishes a static site; simple, portable and resolutely not collaborative.

facts.install: Install the native Windows/macOS package or Linux AppImage
facts.dataFormat: Source content and media in a user-selected local Sites Location; publishing generates static HTML, CSS and assets, with optional local backup archives
facts.gapVsPaid: Publii is a single-user desktop publisher, so it lacks Typedream's instant browser collaboration and text-first flow.
facts.setupBlocker: Publishing still needs separate hosting plus SFTP, GitHub or Netlify credentials/configuration

alternatives.name: Silex
alternatives.desc: A simple visual site builder with static export; not text-first, but still understandable without a developer.

facts.install: Use the hosted editor with a GitLab login, install the desktop alpha, or run the official Docker setup
facts.engines: Optional desktop MCP workflow can connect to Ollama, OpenCode, Goose or Claude Code
facts.dataFormat: Project JSON and assets in GitLab, FTP or local storage; publishing produces ordinary static HTML, CSS and JavaScript
facts.gapVsPaid: Silex is canvas-first rather than text-first, making quick document-like landing pages slower to compose.
facts.setupBlocker: The stable hosted route starts with a GitLab account; the desktop build is still labelled alpha

alternatives.name: Webstudio
alternatives.desc: A polished visual builder for simple sites if you can tolerate self-hosting for a free custom domain.

facts.install: Hosted signup or desktop app; alternatively export the project or deploy the self-hosted builder/site
facts.engines: Webstudio Inception AI and MCP integrations; the hosted model provider is not named in official documentation
facts.dataFormat: Projects and assets live in Webstudio Cloud when hosted there; export/self-host routes produce source or static assets under the user's deployment
facts.gapVsPaid: Webstudio is much more CSS-heavy than Typedream's text-first blocks and requires self-deployment for a free custom domain.
facts.setupBlocker: The free cloud plan publishes only to a Webstudio subdomain; a free custom domain requires export or self-hosting

rejectedAlternatives.name: GrapesJS
rejectedAlternatives.desc: A toolkit for someone building Typedream, not Typedream for someone building a site.

notes: Editorial comparison targets the Launch plan and a single-site builder DIY substitute. Recheck price before merge.
prompt:
Build a personal replacement for Typedream in an empty repository.
Use Next.js 15, TypeScript, Tailwind CSS, SQLite, Drizzle ORM, and static export; do not offer alternative stacks.
The core loop is: assemble a simple responsive landing site from text-first blocks, edit copy and media, preview breakpoints, and publish a static site to a user-owned target.
Make the first run work locally with one documented command.
Store all user data locally by default and make export straightforward.
Put secrets in .env, ship .env.example, and never commit credentials.
Provide a section library for hero, proof, features, pricing, FAQ, and footer blocks.
Use a constrained design-token system rather than arbitrary CSS controls.
Allow inline text editing and local image upload with responsive optimization.
Preview desktop, tablet, and mobile widths and surface overflow errors.
Persist projects in SQLite and support a portable JSON export.
Generate a clean static Next.js output and document deployment to one target.
Include clear empty, loading, success, and recoverable error states.
Add input validation, safe filenames, and graceful handling of unavailable APIs.
Write focused tests for the core transformation and one end-to-end happy path.
Create a README with setup, architecture, permissions, data location, and backup steps.
Do not add accounts, billing, telemetry, analytics, or a hosted control plane.
Deliberately leave out a plugin marketplace.
Deliberately leave out multi-tenant managed hosting.
Deliberately leave out advanced ecommerce, memberships, and agency billing.
Finish by running the tests and listing the exact commands used.
